originalTitle: Households near new pylons to get £250 taken off annual energy bills
summary: Discounts confirmed near more than 40 locations across Great Britain amid biggest upgrade to electricity grid since 1960s
content: Households living near new power pylons will have £250 a year taken off their energy bills as the UK government prepares to push ahead with more than 40 grid upgrade projects across the country. The government has promised hundreds of thousands of homes living within 500 metres of new grid infrastructure a saving of up to £2,500 on their energy bills over 10 years in return for “hosting vital infrastructure” which will help the UK transition away from fossil fuels. One of the biggest grid upgrade drives since the 1960s will mean communities in over 40 locations across the country will be eligible for the payments as the government hopes to prevent a backlash against increased the building of pylons and substations. Michael Shanks, the energy minister, said the multibillion-pound upgrades, which will be paid for through household energy bills, were “a vital part of how we deliver secure, homegrown energy and unlock economic growth across the country”. “It is a moment of national renewal – upgrading what was built largely in the 1960s for the modern age and is our route to bringing down electricity bills for households across the country,” he said. “It’s vital we build again as a country and we are determined those communities which host pylons should benefit which is why we’re bringing down the energy bills of those hosting this vital national infrastructure,” Shanks added. Grid companies are expected to spend up to £77bn over five years to build the new networks and power lines needed to carry renewable electricity, often generated offshore or in more remote parts of the country, to urban areas with high electricity demand. The government confirmed the sweetener for local communities near these projects after ruling out proposals to run the new cables underground. It said that research, commissioned by the department for energy and net zero (DESNZ), found that “building pylons remains the most cost-effective way of upgrading Britain’s outdated electricity networks” and would provide “the best value for bill-payers”. The eligible households can expect to receive their energy bill discountsautomatically every six months via their energy supplier. The discounts will begin next year. The government has also called on grid companies including National Grid, SSE and Scottish Power to plough millions into a fund which will be used to support projects which benefit the local communities. Some of the biggest beneficiaries will be those living close to National Grid’s Bramford-to-Twinstead grid reinforcement project which will receive more than £4m in payments to fund community projects. In Scotland, communities near Scottish Power’s Chirmorie overhead line project would be eligible for about £2.4m of community benefit funding. At present, constraints in the country’s ageing grid network mean that wind and solar farms are paid to stop generating electricity if there is not enough demand in the local area to absorb the power. The electricity system operator also pays gas plants to fire up to meet demand, and buys electricity imported from the continent via high-voltage power cables. These payments are expected to total £3bn by 2030.
chineseTitle: 新铁塔附近的家庭年度能源费用可减免250英镑
chineseSummary: 英国自 20 世纪 60 年代以来最大规模的电网升级已在英国近 40 多个地点确认折扣
chineseContent: 随着英国政府准备在全国范围内推进 40 多个电网升级项目，居住在新输电塔附近的家庭每年的能源费用将减少 250 英镑。政府承诺，居住在新电网基础设施 500 米范围内的数十万家庭将在 10 年内节省高达 2,500 英镑的能源费用，以换取“托管重要基础设施”，这将有助于英国摆脱化石燃料。这是自 20 世纪 60 年代以来最大的电网升级计划之一，这意味着全国 40 多个地点的社区将有资格获得这笔付款，因为政府希望防止对增加铁塔和变电站建设的强烈抵制。能源部长迈克尔·尚克斯表示，数十亿英镑的升级将通过家庭能源账单支付，是“我们如何提供安全的本土能源和释放全国经济增长的重要组成部分”。他说：“这是国家复兴的时刻——对 20 世纪 60 年代主要建设的建筑进行升级改造，使其适应现代生活，也是我们降低全国家庭电费的途径。”尚克斯补充说：“作为一个国家，我们重新建设至关重要，我们决心那些拥有电塔的社区应该受益，这就是为什么我们要降低那些拥有这一重要国家基础设施的社区的能源费用。”电网公司预计将在五年内花费高达 770 亿英镑来建设新的网络和电力线路，以将可再生电力（通常来自海上或该国更偏远的地区）输送到电力需求较高的城市地区。在排除了在地下铺设新电缆的提议后，政府确认了这些项目附近当地社区的甜味剂。它是
